sub: How to keep the talent you trained

steps.title: Spot potential early
steps.tip: Decide early, so the talk is not rushed in the final week.

steps.title: Give them a real project
points: One project they own start to finish
A chance to present the results
steps.tip: Real ownership shows you how they would do the job.

steps.title: Talk about the future
points: Share which roles could open up
steps.tip: Good interns often take the first firm offer. Talk early.

steps.title: Make a clear offer
points: Put the role and start date in writing
Explain what changes after the internship
steps.tip: Don't rush them. Pressure loses good people.

steps.title: Plan the first months
points: Keep the same mentor if you can
Set goals for the first 90 days
Celebrate the move with the team
steps.tip: A smooth handover keeps their momentum going.

cta_title: Ready to keep your best intern?
cta_sub: Start the conversation before their last week.
post_title: From Intern to Full-Time Hire: 5 Moves

captions.linkedin:
Your best intern could be your next hire. 5 moves to make it happen.

1. Spot potential early: ownership, attitude to feedback
2. Give them a real project they own
3. Talk about the future, honestly and early
4. Make a clear offer in writing and give them time to decide
5. Plan the first months: same mentor, 90-day goals

Internships are one of the best ways to find your next graduate hire.
